concepts.label: Half-secure XDCR replication
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the security level securing only the administrator password sent to the remote cluster, not the replicated data itself, via SCRAM-SHA or (for pre-5.5 targets) TLS. Sibling of the extraction-layer xdcr:fully-secure-replication (minted round 20, xdcr-security-and-networking.json, from the reference tree's certificate-chain discussion). This page is the first in the corpus to name BOTH security levels as a closed, named two-member choice ('The following security-levels are supported: _Half-secure_... _Fully_ secure...') - the reference tree only ever discussed the fully-secure/TLS mechanics in isolation, never the half/full choice as a scheme.

concepts.label: Fully secure XDCR replication
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted in server/8.0/xdcr-reference/xdcr-security-and-networking.json (round 20). This page restates the same definition in the Web Console procedure guide's own words.

concepts.label: SCRAM (Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted in server/8.0/learn/security/authentication-overview.json. This page's own 'SCRAM-SHA' password-hashing mechanism for half-secure replication is the same family concept applied specifically to XDCR.

relations.subject: xdcr:reference
relations.evidence:
The following security-levels are supported: 

* _Half-secure_: Secures the specified password only: it does not secure data.

relations.subject: xdcr:reference
relations.evidence: _Fully_ secure: Handles both authentication and data-transfer via TLS.

relations.subject: xdcr:half-secure-replication
relations.evidence: By hashing with SCRAM-SHA, when the destination cluster is running Couchbase Enterprise Server 5.5 or later.

relations.subject: xdcr:half-secure-replication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (availableSince) - marks the version at which SCRAM-SHA became the password-securing mechanism, with TLS as the pre-5.5 fallback
relations.evidence: By hashing with SCRAM-SHA, when the destination cluster is running Couchbase Enterprise Server 5.5 or later.

relations.subject: xdcr:half-secure-replication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresCapability) - only required for the pre-5.5 TLS fallback path, not the SCRAM-SHA path
relations.evidence: The root certificate of the destination cluster must be provided, for a successful TLS connection to be achieved.

relations.subject: xdcr:fully-secure-replication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresCapability) - loose fit; the minimum source-side version required for Capella's CA to be auto-trusted
relations.evidence: CAs used by the Couchbase cloud data-platform, _Capella_, are automatically trusted, when _fully secure_ XDCR connections are made to Capella databases from Couchbase Enterprise Server 7.2 or later versions, using Couchbase Web Console or the REST API.

relations.subject: xdcr:fully-secure-replication
relations.evidence: For step-by-step instructions, see [Enable Fully Secure Replications](enable-full-secure-replication.md).

notable_absence.finding: No role is named on this security-configuration page - consistent with round 20's own finding on xdcr-security-and-networking.json that XDCR 'security' throughout the corpus means network/transport/certificate mechanics, never RBAC.

cross_component_finding: SUPPLIES THE MISSING HALF OF ROUND 20'S SECURITY-LEVEL VOCABULARY. xdcr-security-and-networking.json minted xdcr:fully-secure-replication from the reference tree's certificate-chain discussion but had no occasion to name a half-secure counterpart, since that reference page's own scope was TLS/mTLS mechanics only. This Web Console procedure page is where the half/full CHOICE itself - the thing an administrator actually picks in the Add/Edit Remote Cluster dialog - is named and defined, exactly the kind of admin-procedure-only vocabulary this batch's brief predicted for the security pages specifically.
